Police Station, Belagavi For The Offences Punishable
Under Sections 403 And 420 Read With Section 34 Of Ipc,
So Far As It Relates To The Petitioners Herein.
 This Petition Coming On For Admission This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order
Though the matter is listed for admission, with the consent from both the sides, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. This petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking to quash the charge sheet and the entire proceedings initiated in C.C.No.457/2017 on the file of IV JMFC, Belagavi.
3. The respondent-police have filed a charge sheet against four accused persons alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 403, 420 read with Section 34 of IPC.

The substance of the accusations made in the charge sheet is that, on 21.01.2017 on credible information the PSI of CCIB Unit, Belagavi kept a watch near the APMC Market Yard and found two persons standing suspiciously holding a plastic bag on their shoulders.

When the raiding team surrounded them, one of them escaped from the spot, whereas, petitioner No.1-Ganghadar @ Sanju S/o Rudrappa Hadaginhal was caught and on search he was found in possession of seven packets of milk powder weighing 1 Kg each and twelve packets weighing  Kg each.
Those packets were seized under a mahazar.

A FIR was registered and after investigation, the charge sheet was laid against four accused persons alleging that all the four accused persons were involved in the sale of milk powder which was supplied by the Government under Ksheera Bhagya Scheme.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the allegations made against the petitioners do not attract the offences under Sections 403 or 420 of IPC.
The material produced by the prosecution indicate that petitioner No.1 was found in possession of the milk powder.
The possession of the said milk powder is not an offence under any provisions of law much less under Sections 403 or 420 of IPC.
There are no allegations whatsoever attracting the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
Insofar as the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are concerned, there is absolutely no material to show their involvement in the alleged offences.

Considering the very same material, this Court has Shri Ganghadar @ Sanju S/O. Rudrappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157716922/
2 already quashed the proceedings in respect of accused No.4 in Criminal Petition No.101472/2017.

sentences.text: The present petitioners also stand at par with accused No.4 against whom identical allegations are made.
The prosecution of the petitioners therefore is wholly illegal and sheer abuse of the process of Court and hence, the learned counsel seeks for quashing the said proceedings.

5. Learned HCGP fairly concedes that the prosecution has not collected any material insofar as the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are concerned in order to support the accusations made against them for the alleged offences under Sections 403 and 420 of IPC.

However, insofar as petitioner No.1 namely accused No.1 is concerned, he submits that the investigation conducted by the prosecution reveal that he was in possession of milk packets which were not meant for sale in the market.

The sale of milk powder supplied under the schemes formulated by the Government is an offence and therefore,
the prosecution of petitioner No.1 is in accordance with law and no illegallity or abuse of process of law is involved in the instant case sofar as accused No.1 is concerned and hence seeks for dismissal of the petition.
6. The argument of the learned HCGP in my view does not find support from any provisions of the law.
The learned HCGP has not brought to my notice any provision of law, or Order or Notification issued by the Government prohibiting possession of milk packets supplied under the Ksheera Bhagya Scheme.
The argument proceeds on the assumption that the milk packets found in the possession of accused No.1 were intended for sale.

But, unfortunately, no material whatsoever is available on record to suggest that accused No.1 was either involved in the sale of the said milk packets or that the said milk packets were offered for sale.
The allegations in the charge sheet are confined to the possession of the milk packets.

7. In order to make out an offence under Section 403 IPC, the prosecution is required to establish that the property is misappropriated or converted to the use of the accused and secondly the misappropriation or conversion must be with dishonest intention.

Merely because the accused was found in possession of the milk packets without any evidence of dishonest conversion, the allegations made against the accused are not sufficient to attract the offence under Section 403 or 420 IPC.

Except the evidence relating to seizure of the milk packets, the prosecution has not collected any evidence either in proof of misappropriation or conversion of the milk packets to the use of the accused.
The learned HCGP has not been able to point out as to how the possession of the milk powder could be an offence under Section 403 of IPC or any other provision of law.
It is not the case of the prosecution that the possession of the milk powder is violative of the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
No action appears to have been taken against the accused for violation of the Rules or Regulations issued under the said Act.
Therefore, in my view, the prosecution initiated against the petitioners is bad in law and therefore cannot be sustained.
8. Hence, the following order:-
The petition is allowed.
The proceedings pending on the file of IV JMFC, Belgavi in C.C.No.457/2017 are quashed.
